RequestId.description: The request's id: the inbound `X-Request-Id` when it is 1 to 128 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`, otherwise a fresh `req_...` id. Error bodies repeat it as `request_id`. Quote it when contacting support.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent on every 429.

Retry-After-long.description: Deprecated: read `Retry-After`. Seconds to wait, when the per-minute IP limit tripped.

Retry-After-short.description: Deprecated: read `Retry-After`. Seconds to wait, when the per-second IP limit tripped.

X-RateLimit-Limit-long.description: Requests allowed per minute from this client IP (600).

X-RateLimit-Limit-short.description: Requests allowed per second from this client IP (20).

X-RateLimit-Remaining-long.description: Requests left in the current one-minute window.

X-RateLimit-Remaining-short.description: Requests left in the current one-second window.

X-RateLimit-Reset-long.description: Seconds until the one-minute window resets.

X-RateLimit-Reset-short.description: Seconds until the one-second window resets.

email.description: Address to suppress. Once listed, sends to it are dropped before delivery.

reason.description: Why it was suppressed. Free text, for the operator reading the list later.

dry_run.description: `true`: return the plan and change nothing. `false`: apply the plan and return what was written.

include_dmarc.description: Also add the recommended DMARC record (`_dmarc.<fqdn>` `v=DMARC1; p=none;`). Only ever planned when no DMARC policy applies at the domain or its organisational domain; an existing policy is never touched, whatever this says.

provider.description: The DNS provider that hosts the zone.

token.description: A short-lived API token for the provider, used for this request only and never stored, logged or returned. Cloudflare: an API token limited to this one zone with the **Zone → DNS → Edit** permission and a short expiry. DigitalOcean: a personal access token with custom scopes `domain:read`, `domain:create`, `domain:update` and a 1-hour expiry. Revoke it once the apply is done.

zone.description: The zone at the provider (the domain or one of its parents). Defaults to the closest parent zone the token can see.

raw.description: User-set values only (null when the workspace has never customised). Null fields signal "not customised — falling through to default".

resolved.description: Fully-resolved tokens every render uses. The frontend reads this for previews so what the editor shows == what recipients get.

recipients.description: Who a send started now would reach: segment ∩ topic subscribers − unsubscribed − suppressed.

segment_contacts.description: Everyone in the segment, before the exclusions. Null without a segment.

canceled.description: Not sent because the broadcast was canceled.

clicked.description: Clicked a link at least once. Counted once click tracking is enabled; 0 until then.

complained.description: Marked as spam by the recipient.

delivered.description: Accepted by the recipient server (a provider `Delivery` event).

failed.description: Could not be sent (`error_code` on the recipient).

opened.description: Opened at least once. Counted once open tracking is enabled for the workspace; 0 until then.

pending.description: Not handed to the mail provider yet.

recipients.description: Recipients the audience froze to when the send started.

skipped.description: Left out at send time: suppressed, or unsubscribed after the audience froze.

unsubscribed.description: Recipients who unsubscribed (globally, or from the broadcast topic) since the send started.

canceled_at.description: When the broadcast was canceled; null when it was not.

completed_at.description: When sending finished; null until then.

counts.description: Null on a draft or a broadcast still scheduled.

created_at.description: When the broadcast was created.

failure_reason.description: Why the broadcast stopped on its own (its segment or topic was deleted).

from.description: Null on a draft that uses the workspace default sender.

html.description: Inline HTML body; null when a template is used.

name.description: Internal name of the broadcast (not shown to recipients).

scheduled_at.description: When the broadcast is scheduled to go out; null when not scheduled.

segment_id.description: Null when only a topic targets it, or the segment was deleted.

started_at.description: When the audience froze and sending began.

status.description: `draft`: editable. `scheduled`: waiting for `scheduled_at`. `sending`: going out. `sent`: every recipient handled. `canceled`: stopped before the end.

subject.description: Subject line; null until set (or when the template supplies it).

template_name.description: Template the broadcast renders; null when it has its own content.

text.description: Plain-text body; null when only HTML or a template is used.

topic_id.description: Topic the broadcast is sent on; recipients who opted out of it are skipped. Null for none.

updated_at.description: When the broadcast was last changed.

contact_id.description: Null when the contact was deleted since.

error.description: Human-readable reason the recipient was not sent to; null when sent.

error_code.description: Machine-readable reason the recipient was not sent to; null when sent.

sent_at.description: When the email to this recipient was sent; null until then.

status.description: `pending`: waiting. `sending`: being handed off. `sent`: handed to the provider (see `message_status`). `skipped`: left out at send time. `failed`: see `error_code`. `canceled`: the broadcast was canceled first.

default_rate_per_minute.description: Default sending rate for new broadcasts, in emails per minute.

effective_rate_per_minute.description: What a broadcast without its own rate is sent at.

rate_per_minute.description: The workspace campaign pace; null uses the default.

clicks.description: How many clicks the link got.

data.description: Most clicked first, at most 100. Empty until click tracking is enabled for the workspace.

return_to.description: URL the workspace user should land on after the GitHub OAuth flow completes. Must be a same-origin or productcraft.co URL — anything else is rejected to keep the callback from being an open-redirect.

authorize_url.description: Browser redirects here to start the GitHub OAuth flow.

consented_at.description: When the consent was given. Defaults to now.

source.description: Where the consent came from, for your records and for an audit: a form name, a checkout checkbox, a double opt-in confirmation.

created_at.description: When the event happened (the same on every retry).

domain_id.description: The sending domain the event is about; null for workspace-level events (suppression, contacts, settings) and when the domain is unknown. Absent on "Send test" deliveries.

id.description: The event id, also sent as `webhook-id`; the same on every retry and replay.

test.description: Present and true only on a delivery made by "Send test"; its `data` is the catalogue example.

type.description: The event type. Switch on it to narrow the event.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the event belongs to, so you can route without opening `data`. Absent on "Send test" deliveries.

errors.description: The first 100 problems, with line numbers.

updated_count.description: Rows that updated an existing contact.

fallback_value.description: Value used for a contact that has no value for this property; null for none.

default_subscription.description: Whether a contact who never chose is subscribed (`opt_in`) or not (`opt_out`).

description.description: Optional longer text shown under the name on the unsubscribe page.

name.description: Display name of the topic, shown on the unsubscribe page.

reason.description: Why: `opted_in`, `default_with_consent`, or, when not subscribed, `unsubscribed` (global), `opted_out`, `no_consent` (an `opt_in` topic but no recorded consent), `not_opted_in` (an `opt_out` topic).

subscription.description: The contact's own choice; null when it never made one.

visibility.description: `public` topics appear on the unsubscribe page; `private` ones do not.

contact_id.description: The contact these subscriptions belong to.

data.description: Every topic of the workspace with this contact's subscription to it.

from.description: Sender: `ada@example.com` or `Ada <ada@example.com>`, on an active sending domain of this workspace. Omit to use the workspace default sender (resolved and fixed when the broadcast is sent).

html.description: Inline HTML body (Handlebars), instead of `template_name`. Rendered per recipient with the contact as data (`{{first_name}}`, `{{email}}`, property keys, or `{{contact.plan}}`). Must contain `{{{unsubscribe_url}}}` before the broadcast can be sent.

name.description: Internal name of the broadcast (not shown to recipients).

rate_per_minute.description: Messages per minute for this broadcast, 1 to 300. Omit to use the workspace setting (`GET /broadcast-settings`, default 120). Campaign mail has its own limit, separate from the transactional send limit.

scheduled_at.description: Default send time used by `POST .../send` when it gives none.

segment_id.description: Target segment. With `topic_id` too, the audience is both.

subject.description: Subject (Handlebars). Required with `html`; with `template_name`, overrides the template subject.

template_name.description: A saved template of this workspace, instead of `html`.

text.description: Optional plain-text part (Handlebars). Derived from the HTML when omitted. When given, it must contain `{{{unsubscribe_url}}}` too.

topic_id.description: Target topic: only contacts subscribed to it (opted in, or default `opt_in` with recorded consent).

consent.description: A marketing consent the contact gave you. Without one, the contact receives only topics it explicitly opted in to (`topics`, or `PATCH .../topics`).

first_name.description: The contact's first name, available as `{{first_name}}` in templates.

last_name.description: The contact's last name, available as `{{last_name}}` in templates.

properties.description: Custom properties, keyed by a defined contact property (`POST /contact-properties`). Values must match its type.

unsubscribed.description: Global unsubscribe: the contact receives no topic mail and no mail with an unsubscribe link. Transactional mail is unaffected.

consent_source.description: Recorded as `consent_source` on consented rows that have no `consent_source` column value. Defaults to `import`.

csv.description: The CSV file content, UTF-8, at most 10 MB and 100,000 rows. The first line is a header with an `email` column. Optional columns: `first_name`, `last_name`, `unsubscribed` (true/false), `consent` (true/false), `consented_at` (ISO 8601), `consent_source`, and any defined contact property key. Headers are case-insensitive (`First Name` works). Other columns are ignored and reported. A row is consented only when it says so (`consent` true, or a `consented_at` date); every other imported contact starts without consent and receives only topics it later opts in to.

on_conflict.description: `upsert` updates an existing contact (provided fields; properties merge); `skip` leaves existing contacts unchanged. Either way an import never re-subscribes a contact that unsubscribed and never overrides a topic opt-out.

topic_ids.description: Opt the consented rows in to these topics (existing opt-outs win).

fallback_value.description: The value to use when a contact has none. Must match `type`.

key.description: The property key: lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, up to 50 characters. Use it as a CSV column header and as a key of `properties` on a contact. Contact fields (`email`, `first_name`, …) are reserved.

type.description: Value type. Fixed once created.

capabilities.description: Resend's shape of `intent`: `sending` defaults to `enabled`, `receiving` to `disabled`; at least one must be enabled.

click_tracking.description: Only `false` for now; `true` is refused with 422 `TRACKING_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

custom_return_path.description: Resend's name for `mail_from_subdomain`: the custom MAIL FROM (return-path) label, `bounce` → `bounce.<fqdn>`. Sending domains only; defaults to `bounce`. Refused with 409 `MAIL_FROM_HOST_IN_USE` when that host already has records that are not ours.

fqdn.description: Fully qualified domain name. Required unless `name` is sent.

intent.description: How the workspace plans to use this domain; drives which DNS records gate verification. Defaults to `send` (Resend's default: sending on, receiving off). Same as `capabilities`; send one or the other, or both in agreement.

name.description: Resend's name for `fqdn`. Send either; both must agree when both are sent.

open_tracking.description: Only `false` for now; `true` is refused with 422 `TRACKING_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

region.description: The AWS region to send from. Every domain of this deployment sends from the same region (`region` on any domain, e.g. `eu-north-1`); any other value is refused with 422 `REGION_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

tls.description: `opportunistic` only for now (TLS whenever the receiver offers it); `enforced` is refused with 422 `TLS_ENFORCED_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

tracking_subdomain.description: Not available yet: any value is refused with 422 `TRACKING_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

domain_id.description: Domain ID.

local_part.description: Local part of the address (portion before @)

description.description: Optional description of who is in the segment.

name.description: Unique per workspace.

rule.description: Omit for a static segment (add contacts with `POST .../contacts/{contact}/segments/{segment_id}`). Set it for a rule segment: its members are the contacts that match, evaluated whenever the segment is read. The type is fixed once created.

email_to.description: Optional: email the link to these people (whoever manages the DNS). At most 5 recipients per domain per UTC day and 20 per workspace, counted across all links; over that the request is refused with 429 and no link is created. Each recipient gets their own email from ProductCraft with the domain name, the link and its expiry.

expires_in_days.description: Days until the link stops working (1–7).

default_subscription.description: `opt_in`: contacts receive the topic unless they opt out — but only contacts with a recorded consent (`consent` on the contact, or an import row that asserted it). `opt_out`: contacts receive it only after opting in. Fixed once created.

description.description: One line under the name on the unsubscribe page.

name.description: Shown to recipients on the unsubscribe page.

visibility.description: `public` topics are listed on the unsubscribe page; `private` ones are not (a recipient can still leave one from its own link).

domain_id.description: Only events about this domain. Omit or null for every event of the workspace.

enabled.description: Send `false` to create it switched off.

event_types.description: Event types from `GET …/webhooks/event-types`. Empty or omitted means every event, including types added later. Older names (`message.sent`, `message.delivered`, `message.deferred`, `message.bounced`, `message.complained`, `message.failed`) are still accepted; an endpoint subscribed under one receives the event with that name as its `type`.

events.description: Older name for `event_types`, accepted and returned until the legacy webhook routes are retired (Sunset: 2027-01-15). Send one of the two.

url.description: Where to send events: an absolute https:// URL on a public host.

api_url.description: The same link as JSON (`GET /v1/public/domain-setup/{token}`), for scripts.

created_at.description: When the link was created.

domain_id.description: The domain the link shares the DNS setup of.

emailed_to.description: Recipients the email was queued for (an address whose email could not be queued is left out).

emailed_to_count.description: How many recipients the link was emailed to.

last_viewed_at.description: Last time the public page was opened (updated at most once a minute).

revoked_at.description: When the link was revoked; null while not revoked.

status.description: `active` until `expires_at` or until revoked.

url.description: The page to send: a read-only setup page with the records, live status and downloads, no account needed. Shown only in this response; it cannot be retrieved again (only a hash is stored). When the request carried an `Idempotency-Key`, a retry with the same key within 24 h returns this same response.

address.description: The default From: a bare address (`hello@acme.com`) or a display name plus the address (`Acme <hello@acme.com>`). Template sends with no `from` go out with it.

domain_id.description: The workspace domain the address is on; null when that domain was deleted after the default was set.

domain_status.description: The domain's live `verification_status` (the same value `GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/domains/{domainId}` returns), or `deleted` when the domain was removed. The shared `SenderDomainStatus` enum, which Auth and Waitlist use too; Mail never answers `not_found` here.

verified.description: Whether mail from this address sends right now: the domain is `verified`, or `temporary_failure` (a record went missing within the 72 h grace). When false, sends that use the default are refused with 422 `from_domain_not_verified` or `domain_not_verified_by_provider`.

count.description: Template sends skipped since the setting last changed because they named no `from` and no default sender was set. Reset to 0 by every PUT.

last_at.description: When the most recent skip happened; null when none ever did.

last_template.description: The template of the most recent skipped send.

detail.description: The remote diagnostic that matched a block signature.

dmarc.description: The DMARC policy that governs the domain, from its last DNS check; null before the first.

status.description: Verification status of the domain.

block_signals.description: Diagnostics that matched a known reputation-block signature.

confirmed.description: Messages with recipient-side evidence of arrival. Zero across the estate today — nothing emits that evidence yet, and reporting zero is the honest answer rather than assuming success.

domains.description: Each sending domain with its DMARC grade. Gmail and Yahoo require DMARC from bulk senders, so a domain with `dmarc.location = none` is a deliverability risk regardless of the verdict.

left_queue.description: Messages handed off for delivery in the window.

queued.description: Messages still waiting to be handed off.

summary.example: 80 message(s) were handed off and none has been confirmed as arriving.

verdict.description: Overall verdict. `unconfirmed` is NOT a synonym for healthy: it means mail was handed off and nothing came back in either direction, which is the shape a blackholed sender makes. `healthy` requires positive recipient-side evidence.

adkim.description: DKIM alignment mode (`r` relaxed, the default).

aspf.description: SPF alignment mode (`r` relaxed, the default).

host.description: Name the governing record was found at.

location.description: `subdomain`: `_dmarc.<fqdn>` exists. `organizational`: inherited from a parent domain. `none`: no policy applies.

policy.description: Policy that applies to mail from this domain (`sp=` when inherited from a parent that sets it).

warning.description: What needs attention, if anything (e.g. no policy at all: Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender rules require DMARC).

code.description: `spf_multiple`: more than one SPF record at the name (permerror). `spf_merge`: an SPF record exists, merge ours into it. `spf_lookup_limit`: the merged SPF needs more than 10 DNS lookups. `cname_at_host`: a CNAME occupies the name. `mail_from_mx_multiple`: the MAIL FROM host has other MX records. `dmarc_duplicate`: two DMARC records. `dkim_selector_taken`: a different DKIM key at our selector. `mx_foreign`: inbound mail for the name currently goes elsewhere (informational).

message.description: One sentence on what is wrong and how to fix it.

purpose.description: What the conflicting record is for.

severity.description: `blocking`: the record cannot work until this is fixed. `warning`: works, but read this.

suggested_value.description: The value to publish instead (e.g. a merged SPF record), when there is one.

create.description: Records that would be (or were) created.

skip.description: Records already correct and left as they are.

update.description: Records that would be (or were) updated.

action.description: `create`: a new record is added. `update`: an existing SPF record absorbs our mechanism (the only record we ever modify; see `before`/`after`). `skip`: already in place, or nothing to do (see `note`).

after.description: The record after the apply (MX as `<priority> <host>`). For `skip`, the same as `before`.

before.description: `update`: the record being replaced. `skip`: the record already satisfying ours. Null for `create`.

conflicts.description: Conflicts on this record. Any `blocking` one refuses the apply (409).

existing.description: What the zone holds today at `host` for this record type (TXT unquoted and joined; MX as `<priority> <host>`).

name_relative.description: Name relative to the provider zone (`@` for the apex).

note.description: Why a record is skipped, when it is not simply already in place.

optional.description: A recommended extra the caller opted into (`include_dmarc`).

required.description: Whether this record gates the domain going `active`.

result.description: What happened to this record on an apply; null on a dry run.

ttl.description: TTL (seconds) the record is written with.

type.description: DNS record type.

value.description: The value written (an update: the merged record). For MX, the mail exchanger host; the priority is separate.

applied.description: Whether records were written (false on a dry run).

conflicts.description: Every conflict in the plan, flattened, with the record it belongs to.

dmarc_available.description: No DMARC policy applies to this domain, so the optional DMARC record can be added (`include_dmarc`).

dns_records.description: After an apply: the result of the DNS check run right away (new records are usually `propagating`). Null on a dry run.

domain_id.description: The domain the records were applied to.

dry_run.description: True when this was a dry run: nothing was written.

plan.description: Each record and what was (or would be) done with it.

provider.description: The DNS provider the records were written to.

warnings.description: `token_scope_broader_than_zone`: the token can see more than this zone; it worked, but revoke it now. `dmarc_lookup_failed`: we could not tell whether a DMARC policy applies, so DMARC was left out. `partially_applied`: some writes failed (see each item's `error`); run it again once fixed, finished records are skipped.

zone.description: The provider zone the records go into.

host.description: Fully qualified DNS name to publish the record at.

purpose.description: What the record is for: `dkim` (signing key; also the ownership proof for sending domains), `mx` (inbound routing, receive/both only), `verification` (ownership token, receive-only domains), `spf` (legacy From-domain SPF, informational), `mail_from_mx` / `mail_from_spf` (custom MAIL FROM host, recommended), `dmarc` (recommended only while no DMARC policy applies to the domain).

required.description: Whether this record must pass before the domain goes `active` for its intent. `false` means informational or recommended: reported, never blocking.

type.description: Record type.

value.description: Record value the customer must publish.

code.description: `spf_multiple`: more than one SPF record at the name (permerror). `spf_merge`: an SPF record exists, merge ours into it. `spf_lookup_limit`: the merged SPF needs more than 10 DNS lookups. `cname_at_host`: a CNAME occupies the name. `mail_from_mx_multiple`: the MAIL FROM host has other MX records. `dmarc_duplicate`: two DMARC records. `dkim_selector_taken`: a different DKIM key at our selector. `mx_foreign`: inbound mail for the name currently goes elsewhere (informational).

message.description: One sentence on what is wrong and how to fix it.

severity.description: `blocking`: the record cannot work until this is fixed. `warning`: works, but read this.

suggested_value.description: The value to publish instead (e.g. a merged SPF record), when there is one.

covered_by.description: DMARC only: when no record is published at `host` and a parent domain's policy applies, the name that policy lives at. There is nothing to publish then: a record at `host` would replace the inherited policy. Null otherwise.

first_verified_at.description: First time this exact record verified.

found.description: Values found at the name for this type, from the authoritative nameservers when reachable (TXT strings joined; MX as `<priority> <host>`).

hint.description: One human sentence about the current state, including propagation timing.
hint.example: Your nameservers already serve it; public resolvers will within ~30 min (the zone's negative-cache TTL is 1800 s).

host.description: Fully qualified name to publish at (no trailing dot).

id.description: Stored record id; null until the record has been checked once.

last_changed_at.description: Last time the state (or the record) changed, or the nameservers stopped serving a published record (a hold: the state stays published for a few minutes while we re-check).

last_checked_at.description: When this record was last checked; null if never.

name_relative.description: Name relative to the zone (`@` for the apex), the form most DNS provider UIs ask for.

purpose.description: `dkim` signing key (also the ownership proof for sending domains); `mx` inbound routing; `verification` ownership token (receive-only); `spf` legacy From-domain SPF; `mail_from_mx` / `mail_from_spf` custom MAIL FROM; `dmarc` policy.

required.description: Whether this record gates the domain going `active`.

state.description: `missing`: not published. `mismatch`: something else is published at that name (see `found`). `conflict`: published, but another record breaks it (see `conflicts`). `propagating`: your nameservers serve it, public resolvers do not yet (see `hint`). `verified`: published and visible.

type.description: DNS record type.

value.description: Value to publish. For MX, the mail exchanger host (priority is separate).

receiving.description: Receiving mail at this domain (MX pointed at ProductCraft).

bounce_rate.description: Bounce rate, 0 to 1: bounced / emails sent (sent, delivered, deferred, bounced, complained — narrower than `sent` above, which also counts failed and suppressed). Null when nothing was sent.

complained.description: Messages the recipient marked as spam, as reported by their mailbox provider.

complaint_rate.description: Complaint rate, 0 to 1: complained / delivered. Null without mail with delivery tracking or when nothing was delivered.

delivered.description: Messages with status `delivered` (a delivery confirmation came back). Same as the deliverability `confirmed`; complained messages are not included here (they are in `GET /emails/metrics`).

delivery_rate.description: Deliverability rate, 0 to 1: delivered (incl. complained) / `tracked` (emails sent with delivery tracking), as `GET /emails/metrics` defines it. Emails that failed to send (`failed`) are not counted. Null when no mail in the window has delivery tracking.

emails.description: Emails sent, exactly as `GET /emails/metrics` counts `sent`: statuses sent, delivered, deferred, bounced and complained. Excludes failed and suppressed, so it can be lower than `sent`. The denominator of `bounce_rate`.

failed.description: Failed to send: messages refused on our side before they reached any recipient's mail server (status `failed`), exactly as `GET /emails/metrics` counts `failed`. Not in `emails` or `tracked`, so never in a rate.

sent.description: Messages that left the queue: sent + delivered + bounced + complained + failed + deferred + suppressed. Same as the deliverability `left_queue`.

suppressed.description: Messages not sent because the recipient is suppressed.

tracked.description: Emails with delivery tracking, exactly as `GET /emails/metrics` counts `tracked`: the denominator of `delivery_rate`.

unconfirmed.description: Messages handed off with nothing back in either direction (status `sent`). Not a synonym for delivered.

metric.description: Messages that left the queue, per UTC day of `created_at` (same statuses as `in_window.sent`).

points.description: Dense and zero-filled: one point per UTC day in the window, oldest first, ending today.

attention_domains.description: Domains whose `verification_status` is `temporary_failure` or `failed`: a required DNS record is missing or wrong and needs fixing. The rest (`domains` minus `verified_domains` minus this) are still pending or disabled.

verified_domains.description: Domains whose `verification_status` is `verified` (active and healthy). A verified domain whose required record went missing (`temporary_failure`) is not counted here; it is in `attention_domains`.

generated_at.description: When these numbers were computed. Responses are cached for up to 60 seconds.

last_activity_at.description: Most recent outbound message `created_at` still on record (30-day retention). Null when none.

created_at.description: When the mailbox was created.

display_name.description: Display name of the mailbox; null for none.

domain_id.description: The domain the mailbox receives on.

local_part.description: The part before the @ of the mailbox address.

owner_account_id.description: Platform account that created the mailbox; null when created with an API key.

status.description: `active` mailboxes receive mail; `disabled` ones reject it.

workspace_id.description: The workspace that owns the mailbox.

content_id.description: Content-ID of an inline attachment; null otherwise.

filename.description: File name of the attachment; null when it has none.

position.description: Position of the attachment in the message, starting at 0; used to download it.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the attachment, hex encoded.

size_bytes.description: Size of the attachment in bytes.

body_preview.description: First 512 bytes of the plaintext body. This is message content, not metadata, so it is only populated for callers holding `mail.message.body.read`; everyone else sees null. The full body is at /:mid/raw, behind the same action.

subject.description: The rendered subject line.

to.description: The `to` field as sent: one address, or the array.

data.description: One status per row, in request order.

cc.description: Cc recipients: one address or an array. Shown in the `Cc` header to every recipient.

data.description: Template data passed into the Handlebars render. Keys are kept exactly as sent.

from.description: Sender. Either a bare address (`hello@acme.com`) or a display name plus the address in angle brackets (`Acme <hello@acme.com>`; quote a name that contains a comma: `"Acme, Inc." <hello@acme.com>`). The display name is at most 200 characters. The address's domain must itself be an active (verified) sending domain of the workspace; a verified subdomain does not cover its parent (with only `mail.acme.com` verified, `hello@acme.com` is refused with 422 `from_domain_not_verified`).

headers.description: Custom headers, as a map of header name to value, kept exactly as sent. Allowed: `X-*` (except `X-SES-*`), `List-Unsubscribe`, `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, `List-Id`, `In-Reply-To` and `References`; at most 50, values up to 998 characters with no line breaks. Any other header (`From`, `To`, `Cc`, `Bcc`, `Subject`, `Date`, `Message-ID`, `DKIM-Signature`, `Return-Path`, `Reply-To`, …) is a 400 `MAIL_HEADER_NOT_ALLOWED`: use the matching field (`reply_to` for `Reply-To`).

idempotency_key.description: Optional per-row idempotency key. Same dedupe namespace as the `Idempotency-Key` request header.

reply_to.description: Reply-To address(es): one address or an array. This is the only way to set `Reply-To`.

subject.description: Optional override for the rendered subject. Falls back to the template subject.

tags.description: Up to 10 `{ name, value }` labels, stored on every message of the send. Filter sends by them with `GET /emails?tag[name]=value`.

to.description: Recipient: one address, or an array of up to 50 (one row, one message per recipient).

topic_id.description: Send as mail on this topic (tasks/mail-api/016). The recipient must be a contact subscribed to the topic: one who opted in, or, for a topic whose `default_subscription` is `opt_in`, one with a recorded consent who has not opted out. Anyone else is refused with 422 `RECIPIENT_SUPPRESSED` and `details.reason` `unsubscribe` (opted out of the topic or unsubscribed from everything) or `no_consent` (never opted in, or not a contact), and an `email.suppressed` event. A topic send carries a one-click unsubscribe link (`{{{unsubscribe_url}}}` in the template) and the `List-Unsubscribe` + `List-Unsubscribe-Post` headers, and goes out on the separate marketing stream. A `topic_id` that is not a topic of this workspace is a 422 `TOPIC_NOT_FOUND`. In a batch, a refused row is `rejected` with that code; the other rows are unaffected.

code.description: Error code for the rejected row.

error.description: Why the row was rejected; absent when accepted.

id.description: Id of the stored message when accepted (`outbound_message.id`, the same id `GET /messages/{id}` and webhook events use); absent on reject. Null only if the message log write failed; the send itself was still queued.

status.description: Whether the row was accepted for sending or rejected.

scheduled_at.description: Send at this time instead of now (the draft `scheduled_at` when omitted; null forces now). The audience is frozen when sending starts, so people who unsubscribe meanwhile are left out.

emails.description: Up to 100 emails, each processed independently: partial success is allowed and every row reports its own `accepted` / `rejected` status.

muted_text_color.description: Muted text color for footers + secondary copy.

primary_color.description: Primary brand color. Used for buttons, links, and accent strokes. Hex string (e.g. #2d29d7).

secondary_color.description: Secondary brand color, typically darker than primary. Used for hover states + secondary accents.

social_links.description: Map of social-platform → URL. Recognized keys: twitter, x, linkedin, github, instagram, facebook, youtube, tiktok, mastodon, bluesky, web. Keys are stored and returned exactly as sent.

from.description: Sender: `ada@example.com` or `Ada <ada@example.com>`, on an active sending domain of this workspace. Omit to use the workspace default sender (resolved and fixed when the broadcast is sent).

html.description: Inline HTML body (Handlebars), instead of `template_name`. Rendered per recipient with the contact as data (`{{first_name}}`, `{{email}}`, property keys, or `{{contact.plan}}`). Must contain `{{{unsubscribe_url}}}` before the broadcast can be sent.

name.description: New internal name.

rate_per_minute.description: Null restores the default (120 per minute).

consent.description: Record a consent, or `null` to withdraw it.

first_name.description: New first name; null clears it.

last_name.description: New last name; null clears it.

properties.description: Merged into the stored properties; a `null` value removes that key.

unsubscribed.description: Set or clear the global unsubscribe.

fallback_value.description: The new fallback value (null clears it). The key and type cannot change.

topics.description: The topics to change, each with its new subscription.

capabilities.description: Resend's shape of `intent`. Omitted fields keep their current value; at least one must stay enabled.

click_tracking.description: Only `false` for now; `true` is refused with 422 `TRACKING_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

dmarc_managed.description: false: do not recommend a `_dmarc` record for this domain (DMARC is managed elsewhere). The policy that applies is still detected and graded in `dmarc_grade`.

dns_provider.description: Identifier from the wizard's provider list. Free-form so we can ship new entries without a migration. NULL clears the choice.

intent.description: Change how the domain is used. On a verified domain, a capability it gains must verify first: its records are checked live and the change is refused with 409 `CAPABILITY_NOT_VERIFIED` (records to publish in `details.records`) until they pass. Dropping receiving is refused with 409 `DOMAIN_HAS_MAILBOXES` while active mailboxes exist (listed in `details.mailboxes`). Same as `capabilities`; send one or the other, or both in agreement.

mail_from_subdomain.description: Custom MAIL FROM label: one DNS label, so `bounce` makes the envelope sender `…@bounce.<fqdn>` and SPF align with the From domain. `null` turns the custom MAIL FROM off (the default return address is used; DKIM still aligns). Sending domains only.

open_tracking.description: Only `false` for now; `true` is refused with 422 `TRACKING_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

tls.description: `opportunistic` only for now (TLS whenever the receiver offers it); `enforced` is refused with 422 `TLS_ENFORCED_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

tracking_subdomain.description: Not available yet: any value is refused with 422 `TRACKING_NOT_AVAILABLE`.

repo_full_name.description: Repository to sync templates from, as `<owner>/<repo>`.

templates_path.description: Directory in the repository that holds the templates (`/` for the root).

status.description: Mailbox status

redact_bodies.description: When true, messages sent from now on are logged without their body (nothing is stored), and /messages/:id/body returns null body_html + body_text even to callers with mail.message.body.read. Turn it on for workspaces whose mail carries single-use links or codes. Turning it off later does not bring back bodies of messages sent while it was on. Defaults to false.

info.description:
Transactional and marketing email for the ProductCraft platform: send email and templates, verify sending and receiving domains, manage contacts, topics, segments and broadcasts, read received mail, and get delivery events by webhook.

## Rate limits

Every `/v1` route is limited per client IP to 20 requests per second and 600 per minute. Each response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit-short`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining-short`, `X-RateLimit-Reset-short` (the one-second window) and the same three with `-long` (the one-minute window). Over either limit the response is `429` with code `RATE_LIMITED` and a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

Sending is also limited per workspace: 60 emails per minute, 600 per hour and 10,000 per day (test sends: 30 per hour, counted separately). A send over a workspace limit is `429` `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`, `ratelimit-limit`, `ratelimit-remaining` and `ratelimit-reset` for the window that tripped, and `details: { window, limit, retry_after }`. In a batch send, a row over the limit is rejected with `RATE_LIMITED` and the other rows are unaffected.

Some routes have their own, tighter limits (domain lookups, DNS checks, exports, share links); each says so in its `429` response.

post.description: The `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` target. A mailbox provider POSTs `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` (form-encoded); the recipient is unsubscribed from the topic the email was sent on, or from all unsubscribable mail when it had no topic, and the answer is a short `200 text/plain`. No confirmation step, as RFC 8058 requires. The hosted page posts `action=unsubscribe` (same effect) or `action=save` with `topic` (repeated, the topic ids to stay subscribed to; unchecked public topics are opted out) and `all=1` (unsubscribe from everything), and gets the page back. Transactional mail (a send with no topic whose template has no unsubscribe link) is never affected. Emits `contact.updated`, and `contact.created` for a recipient who was not a contact yet.

get.description:
Outbound email counts and rates over a range of up to 30 days, in hourly or daily buckets in your time zone, optionally per sending domain, filtered by domain, API key or source. Read-only.

- **Emails** (`sent`): messages that left the queue.
- **Deliverability rate**: delivered / emails sent with delivery tracking. Emails sent before delivery tracking started, or through a custom SMTP relay, are confirmed at hand-off only, so for them `delivered` is not measured and the rate is `null` (`measured.delivery = false`), never 0.
- **Bounce rate**: bounced / emails. Suppressed recipients never count.
- **Complaint rate**: complained / delivered, from mailbox providers' feedback loops.

Rates are numbers from 0 to 1, or `null` when unmeasured or when the denominator is zero. Template test sends are excluded. Cached for up to 60 seconds.

post.description: Two ways to make retries safe. An `Idempotency-Key` header covers the whole request: a retry with the same key and body within 24 h returns the first response (with `Idempotent-Replay: true`) and sends nothing. A per-row `idempotency_key` covers one message: a later batch, or a `/send`, that repeats a row key replays that row instead of sending it again. Both share one dedupe namespace, so the header key must differ from every row key (400 otherwise).
